done.what: Every Company library action answers a refusal as { error: <the rule> } instead of throwing (a production throw arrives redacted, so the snackbar said 'please try again'). This covers quote templates (rename, delete, restore, bulk restore / forever / empty, set default, publish, submit, request changes, roll back, restore one), task, payment, contract and T&Cs & Notes templates (rename, delete, restore, forever, empty, contract set default, the contract title's rename rule, a too-large body), the price book (update, rename, duplicate, import, bulk change and its Undo, delete, restore, forever, empty, approve, send back, and every section action), folders (create, rename, move, delete, undo) and saveBrand (the Owner or Admin rule plus the entity-in-use refusal). The shared pieces live in the client-safe lib/company/template-rules.ts: Refusal, refuse(), isRefusal(), orThrow() and the new rule strings. lib/company/template-guard.ts now answers a block (changeBlock, defaultBlock, nothingChangeable) and never throws. A bulk Restore now answers { restored, kept } and Delete forever answers { removed, kept }, and when none of the rows are the viewer's the answer is the rule. Price book edits share one internal writeItem, so import, bulk change and Undo check the rule once and keep their History notes. My callers read the answer: the quote template editor (publish, submit, request changes, roll back, Restore on the deleted bar), the task, payment and T&Cs editors (Delete), and the quote editor's T&Cs modal, where a refused delete puts the card back. The quote editor's Save to My Items, its Undo and Save section to My Sections are written to accept an { error } answer already, ready for the items-actions request below.

The server's part: when a folder change is refused, the rule names the folder's maker ('Only Dane, an Owner or an Admin can rename, move or delete this folder'). folder-actions looks up the maker's name and passes it to folderChangeBlockFor. The menu rows and the lead-design wording belong to server and gallery (folder-libraries.ts and the galleries).

The Items table's Sum row now counts only lines that carry a price (a non-zero total). A counted line still at S$0, such as an unpriced finish or a floor waiting for its measured quantity, is counted but not priced. The row reads 'Sum · n priced items' when every line carries a price and 'Sum · n of m priced' otherwise, so the Add-to-quote quote now reads 'Sum · 0 of 3 priced' over S$0.00. Find's subset follows the same rule.

Quote editor at 767px and below. The stray '#n' before Add Item is gone (the phone's Add Item row gets autonumber={false}). 'Additional Discount' takes its own line, with the % | S$ select and the amount box below it at full width. A named discount's word box does the same. Under a finger, the GST switch keeps its gap from 'GST 9%': the house 44px checkbox box (globals, −10 all round) had pulled the track onto the text. The By category head takes its own line above the Share · Margin chips. The Total row keeps the amount's width and drops 'Round Prices' under 'Total' when the two can't share the line; at 320 the link ran into S$49,838.07.

The ITEM cell of each row is now a size container (itemcell). When a cell has 260px of content or less (the 240 cell at 1024 or below, or a column dragged narrow), a section's 'n items' count steps aside first. After that, a section's EMPTY picture well gives its 60px to the name; a picture the section holds stays. The Add-to-quote section name went from 10px wide ('L') to 116px ('Living room · …') at 1024×768 and 768×1024 touch. 1440 is unchanged (the name box measured the same before and after).

At 1024 and below, the active line's Expand sits inside the one-line description box as its end button: absolute, 24×22, no border or shadow, a 16px glyph, and 26px kept clear at the box's end. Before, it hung under the box. Under a finger the touch rules made it position: relative, so it also grew the active row from 80 to 90 and sat on the next row's name. A formatted or full description keeps the hanging button, and 1440 keeps the owner's REG-478 placement.

notDone.why: The remaining suggestion to use a shorter quoteGroupName is not done. It lives in lib/visualizer/outputs.ts (server package). It isn't needed now: the section name reads 'Living room · …' at 1024 touch.

Left as is at 1440: the Expand hangs 2px across the row boundary. That is the owner's REG-478 placement ('hanging under the description box's right end'), and at 1440 it doesn't cover the next row's name.

crossFileRequests.change: updatePriceBookItem now answers PriceBookItem | Refusal, so tsc fails here (line ~367) until this is applied. (1) Add import { refuse, type Refusal } from '@/lib/company/template-rules'. (2) In saveItemToPriceBook, change the return type to Promise<SavedToBook | Refusal>. Replace `if (!runsBook(v)) throw new Error(BOOK_RULE)` with `if (!runsBook(v)) return refuse(BOOK_RULE)`. Replace `if (!cur || cur.deletedAt) throw new Error('item not in the book')` with `return refuse('That item is gone from the price book')`. Replace `const item = await updatePriceBookItem(cur.id, fromLine(i, cur), `Updated from ${q.number}`)` with `const item = await updatePriceBookItem(...same args...); if ('error' in item) return item`. (3) In saveSectionToPriceBook, change the return type to Promise<PriceBookSection | Refusal> (its current type) and replace `if (!runsBook(v)) throw new Error(SECTION_RULE)` with `return refuse(SECTION_RULE)`. (4) In undoSaveToPriceBook, change the return type to Promise<void | Refusal>. Replace `if (block) throw new Error(block)` with `if (block) return refuse(block)`. Replace `throw new Error('already used on another line')` with `return refuse('Another quote line uses it now — it stays in My Items')` (invented copy). Replace `await updatePriceBookItem(cur.id, {...}, 'Undone')` with `const u = await updatePriceBookItem(cur.id, {...}, 'Undone'); if ('error' in u) return u`. components/quotes/editor/items/items-section.tsx already handles all three answers (isRefusal → run() says the rule).

saveContractTemplate answers number | Refusal, so tsc fails at line 64. Add imports: import { isRefusal } from '@/lib/company/template-rules' and import { couldnt, refusalOf } from '@/components/leads/tasks/use-run'. Line 64: `try { setUpdatedAt(await saveContractTemplate(template.id, patch)) } catch {...}` → `try { const r = await saveContractTemplate(template.id, patch); if (isRefusal(r)) snackbar({ message: couldnt('save the template', refusalOf(r.error)) }); else setUpdatedAt(r) } catch {...}`. This covers the title's rename rule and 'The document is too large to save — use a smaller picture'. Line ~120 (Delete confirm): `.then(() => deleteContractTemplate(template.id)).then(() => { router.push(...) }, ...)` → `.then(() => deleteContractTemplate(template.id)).then((r) => { if (isRefusal(r)) { snackbar({ message: couldnt('delete the template', refusalOf(r.error)) }); return } router.push(...) }, ...)`.

saveBrand answers void | Refusal. Line 46: `try { await saveBrand({ kit }); setSaved(kit); snackbar({ message: 'Brand kit saved' }) } catch {...}` → `try { const r = await saveBrand({ kit }); if (isRefusal(r)) { snackbar({ message: couldnt('save the brand kit', refusalOf(r.error)) }); return } setSaved(kit); snackbar({ message: 'Brand kit saved' }) } catch {...}`. Imports: isRefusal from '@/lib/company/template-rules'; couldnt and refusalOf from '@/components/leads/tasks/use-run'. Without this a refusal reads 'Brand kit saved'.

Line 78: `await saveBrand({ details: next }); setDetails(next); setSaved(next); snackbar(...)` → `const r = await saveBrand({ details: next }); if (isRefusal(r)) { snackbar({ message: couldnt('save the company details', refusalOf(r.error)) }); return }` followed by the same three calls. This makes the entity-in-use refusal from reconcileEntities, and the Owner or Admin rule, reach the snackbar whole instead of reading 'Company details saved'. Imports as for brand-kit-view.

In createFolder's catch (line ~124), `catch { snackbar({ message: 'Couldn’t create the folder — please try again' }) }` → `catch (e) { snackbar({ message: couldnt('create the folder', refusalOf(e)) }) }`, importing couldnt and refusalOf from '@/components/leads/tasks/use-run'. LibraryGallery's onCreateFolder throws the rule (newIdOf / orThrow), so the dialog then says 'Couldn’t create the folder — only an Owner or an Admin makes, renames and deletes folders'.

The gallery package has already wrapped these with its exported settle() (tsc is clean there). Check two things. (a) The send-back handler on line ~149 should also settle(sendBackPriceBookItem(...)): its answer can be { error } ('Say what to change — a note goes back with it' or the rule). (b) The bulk Delete / Restore / Undo inside run() on line ~168 should settle() deletePriceBookItems, restorePriceBookItems and undoBulkPriceBook, because each answers { error } when refused. Delete forever / Empty Trash for items and sections now answer { removed, kept }, which the sheet's purgedLine reads.

setDefaultTemplate (line 225), used by the Create Quote modal's tile kebab in lead-quotes.tsx and quotes-workspace.tsx, has no rule check: a Designer can set the studio's default there, which breaks REG-646. Make it delegate: `export async function setDefaultTemplate(templateId: string) { const { setDefaultTemplate: set } = await import('@/app/company/templates-actions'); return set(templateId) }`. The return type becomes Promise<void | Refusal>. The templates-actions version already revalidates every lead (touch). Both callers already go through run(), which says the rule ('Couldn’t set the default template — only an Owner or an Admin sets the studio’s default').
